title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated deepfake videos and fake social media profiles to impersonate a named, real immigration attorney, then offered fraudulent legal services to immigrants seeking residency help. The failure here is impersonation: AI tools were used to fabricate a credible professional identity, complete with the likeness and name of a practicing attorney, and deploy it across multiple social media platforms at scale. The fraud operated entirely outside any legitimate AI deployment, meaning there was no internal system or organization with oversight responsibility for the content being produced.

The attack surface was the gap between the ease of generating convincing video likenesses and the absence of any platform-level verification linking a professional's identity to accounts claiming to represent them. Catching this earlier would have required either proactive detection by social media platforms of synthetic media impersonating real individuals, or a verification system for accounts offering licensed professional services. The volume of fake profiles, nearly 6,500 removed across three platforms, indicates the scammers operated at a scale that manual reporting alone could not address promptly.

It is not established who the scammers are, where they operate from, or whether any law enforcement action has been taken against them. Financial losses reported by victims are described in the coverage but the total extent of harm across all affected individuals is not known.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of artificial intelligence scammers who are using deepfake videos and fake social media profiles featuring his likeness to defraud vulnerable immigrants. The criminals promote fraudulent immigration services, including offering US residency assistance for $2,200 to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office, and he estimates the problem has grown dramatically in recent months.

To combat the fraud, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims through social media videos to contact numbers via WhatsApp, where fraudsters send phony contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to avoid anyone requesting immediate payment. He plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scammers' origins.
